messages.subject: exportData in Splus 8
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

I’m migrating from Splus 6 (32 bit system) to Splus 8 (64 bit system).  Calling the exportData-function under Splus 8 results in too many digits as demonstrated by the following simple example:

x <- sqrt(1:3); x <- round(cbind(x, x), digits = 3)

> x

      [,1]  [,2] 

[1,] 1.000 1.000

[2,] 1.414 1.414

[3,] 1.732 1.732

write.table(x, file = "test8.wrt.txt", sep = "\t", dimnames.write = F, na = "")   yields the expected result, namely 

cat test8.wrt.txt

1       1

1.414   1.414

1.732   1.732

BUT 

exportData(x, file = "test8.txt", quote = F, type = "ASCII", colNames = F,  rowNames = F, delimiter = "\t")   yields 

cat test8.txt

1       1

1.4139999999999999      1.4139999999999999

1.732   1.732

Questions: a) What is the reason for this behavior?  b) How can I force exportData to produce the same output (number of digits) as write.table? options(digits = 3) didn’t seem to help.

Many thanks in advance.

PI

> cor.test(X,Y, method="k")

        Kendall's rank correlation tau 

data:  X and Y 
normal-z = 2.567, p-value = 0.0103 
alternative hypothesis:  tau is not equal to 0 
sample estimates:
       tau 
 0.5606061

Conover gives: 0.5606.

If you wish to check the program:

> cor.test
function(x, y, alternative = "two.sided", method = "pearson")
{
        stop.on.bdObject(x)
        stop.on.bdObject(y)
        if(is(x, "series"))
                x <- as.matrix(x@data)
        if(is(y, "series"))
                y <- as.matrix(y@data)
        vark <- function(x, y)
        {
                # variance of K for Kendall's tau
                ties.x <- as.double(rle(sort(x))$lengths)
                ties.y <- as.double(rle(sort(y))$lengths)
                n <- as.double(length(x))
                t1 <- n * (n - 1) * (2 * n + 5)
                t2 <- sum(ties.x * (ties.x - 1) * (2 * ties.x + 5))
                t3 <- sum(ties.y * (ties.y - 1) * (2 * ties.y + 5))
                v1 <- (t1 - t2 - t3)/18
                t1 <- sum(ties.x * (ties.x - 1) * (ties.x - 2))
                t2 <- sum(ties.y * (ties.y - 1) * (ties.y - 2))
                v2 <- (t1 * t2)/(9 * n * (n - 1) * (n - 2))
                t1 <- sum(ties.x * (ties.x - 1)) * sum(ties.y * 
(ties.y - 1))
                v3 <- t1/(2 * n * (n - 1))
                v1 + v2 + v3
......

                if(imeth == 2) {
                        # a fast, efficient way to compute 
concordant pairs:
                        concordant.sum <- 
sum(unlist(lapply(seq(along = x), function(i, x, y)
                        sum(sign((x[i] - x[1:i]) * (y[i] - y[1:i]))), x, 
y)))
                        # Kendall's tau:
                        coef <- (2 * concordant.sum)/(n * (n - 1))
                        attr(coef, "names") <- "tau"
                        #stddv <- sqrt((n * (n - 1) * (2 * n + 
5))/18)
                        stat <- concordant.sum/sqrt(vark(x, y))
                        # z statistic
                        attr(stat, "names") <- "normal-z"
.......

Ronald

  The value of tau that is reported
is tau, not tau-b, which accounts for ties. The p-value is adjusted for
ties as you suggest.

of positive values is 49, the number of negative values is 12, and the

messages.body_plain:
Good afternoon, folks:

I have a question about the use of the cmprsk package.  Note that this package was developed for the R platform, but it has been ported to the S platform.  

So I guess that my first question is whether there is an R-news list similar to the S-news list where I should also pose this question?

To understand my question, it might help to know what I am trying to do.  I am looking at the impact of a liver organ allocation policy change in UNOS Region 8, comparing various outcomes in the two years before the policy change (era 1) to the two years following the policy change (era 2), using the data from UNOS Regions 6 and 7 as time controls.  Patients on the liver transplant waiting list may have been listed prior to the start of era 1 and may continue on the list up to and into era 2.  

My question:

The functions request a vector ftime (failure/censor times) and a vector fstatus (event and censoring indicators).  Is there a way to engineer a Surv(start, stop, event) counting process approach so that I can accommodate the patients that are listed prior to the start of era1, (i.e, where start > 0)?

Thanks in advance for any help that any of you can give me.

L. G. Hunsicker, M.D.

Professor, Internal Medicine

U. Iowa College of Medicine

Phone:  (319) 356-4763

Fax:  (319) 356-7488

The first problem is the period after the 'BD' instead of
a comma.  (Currently, S+ allows spaces in object
names so 'BD. data' is parsed a a name.  I think it
would be better if it were treated as an error.)  That
fixes your problem below with discrim but not with
lda.

lda's second problem is that its help file lies about the
names of its arguments.  The first 2 are called 'x' and 'y'
but if x is a formula object then y is expected to a data.frame
(like the usual data argument).  If you change 'data=crabs'
to just 'crabs' or 'y=crabs' it will work:

messages.subject_clean: Table and order of rows and columns
messages.body_plain:
I have data frames of predictions and observation of three factors. Call 
these A, B, and c. I've built scoring functions that depend on table() 
returning a contingency table such that column n and row n are always 
for the same observed and predicted factor.  For example, I want table 
to return:

  a    b   c
a  I   J   K
b  L  M  N
c  O  P   Q

where I through Q are integers.

Table provides what I want *almost* all the time. But now I've hit a 
case where the rows and columns do not coincide. For example:

  a   b   c
b  L   M   N
c  O   P   Q
a   I   J   K

What can I do (or use) that will reliably match the order of the rows 
and columns?

Kim Elmore

Dear S-plus users

 

On the historgram graph for an observed 
distribution I want to overlay a normal density distribution 
with the same mean and SD (and later in the analyses produce graphs 
with several other theoretical distributions).

I use the following syntax, BUT the normal 
distribution is displaced on the x-axis (and possibly also on the y-axis). 

The mean of the overlayed normal distribution is 
farther to the right than the observed distribution. This is probably because 
S-plus places the graph to fill the graph sheet for the best 
presentation.

 

HOW do I manage to have 
the overlay distribution placed using the same axis scaling than the observed on 
both the x- and y-axis?

 

(the observed count variable is "mar") 

 

hist(mar, nclass = 10,probability 
=T, xlab = "Number of Mar", ylab = "Proportion of 
mar",main = "MAR",
sub = "with normal 
distribution overlay", density=15)

 

# Density for theoretic normal distribution with 
same mean
par(new = T) # for overlay at the same 
graf
plot(density(rnorm(50000,mean(mar),sqrt(var(mar)))),probability 
=T,type="l", xlab = "", ylab = "",axes = F)

 

Thank you

 

Jan Ivanouw

University of 
Copenhagen

messages.subject: Re: Kendall tau-b
messages.body_plain:
Simona,

Via Google I found this site (Base SAS(R) 9.2 Procedures Guide: 
Statistical Procedures: The CORR Procedure: Kendall's Tau-b 
Correlation Coefficient):

http://support.sas.com/documentation/cdl/en/procstat/59629/HT
ML/default/procstat_corr_sect015.htm

It describes the formulae necessary to compute Kendall's tau b 
and the p-value. You will see that the code in S+ calculates s, V(s) 
and v0, vt, vu, v1 and v2. If you copy the first parts of v0, vt and 
vu then divide by 2 you obtain T0, T1 andT2.

Tau b is then obtained by s/sqrt((T0-T1)(T0-T2))

I hope this helps,

Ronald
